bundle.title: ENG-11245: tolerate transient Vercel errors while polling registrar order
bundle.body:
Why: alert [Win] Route errors on POST /v1/domains/purchase (2026-10-09 ~18:05Z). The purchase succeeded at Vercel (order created), then the first getOrder poll returned a 502 from Vercel. assertRegistrarOrderCompleted threw, the domain was set inactive, and the user's retry hit 409 'no longer available' for the domain they had just bought.

Fix: while polling, a Vercel 5xx/429 is a non-terminal poll and is retried on the normal interval; the last attempt and non-transient errors still throw.

Unrelated to the voter-density alert at the same minute: no election-api errors in the window; failure is a Vercel upstream 502.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes domain purchase completion behavior on Vercel API failures; incorrect classification could delay failure or mask real errors, but scope is limited to registrar order polling.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes a production failure where a successful Vercel registrar purchase could still fail registration when the first `getRegistrarOrder` poll returned a transient upstream error (e.g. 502), which marked the domain **inactive** and left the user unable to retry.
> 
> Adds `isVercelTransientError` on `VercelService` (Vercel **5xx** and **429**). **`assertRegistrarOrderCompleted`** now catches those errors during polling, waits the existing interval, and retries instead of aborting—non-transient errors and the final poll attempt still throw. A unit test covers retry-after-transient-error without setting the domain inactive.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit f2bc49315f79776fe6df218f70d190bbca08d6a4. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

priorFindings.body:
**`isVercelTransientError` misses bare `SDKError` instances, causing test failures and retry bypass.**

In `@vercel/sdk` (Speakeasy-generated), `SDKError` is the base class and `VercelError` extends it — not the reverse. A bare `SDKError` (e.g. a network-level failure the SDK wraps before constructing a domain-specific error) fails `instanceof VercelError`, so:

1. The three test cases at `vercel.service.test.ts` lines 102-106 (`'is true for SDKError 500/502/429'`) will all return `false` instead of `true` and fail.
2. At runtime in the polling loop (`domains.service.ts:1457`), if `getRegistrarOrder` throws an `SDKError` with a 5xx/429 status, `isVercelTransientError` returns `false`, the loop re-throws rather than retrying, and the domain purchase is left in a stranded state — exactly the regression this change was meant to fix.

The `isVercelNotFoundError` method corroborates this: it checks `e instanceof NotFound` separately from `e instanceof VercelError` with an OR, meaning `NotFound` and `VercelError` are siblings under `SDKError`, not in a parent-child relationship that would make the `NotFound` branch redundant.

(Falsification check: if `VercelError` were the base class and `SDKError` extended it, `instanceof VercelError` would catch `SDKError` instances. The separate import paths, the sibling-OR pattern in `isVercelNotFoundError`, and the standard Speakeasy SDK hierarchy all indicate the opposite hierarchy.)

**Poll-exhaustion via transient errors still marks the domain inactive — the core stranded-purchase bug persists.**

When all `REGISTRAR_ORDER_POLL_MAX_ATTEMPTS` polls exhaust with transient errors, the loop exits and the `throw new Error(...)` here propagates to the outer catch (lines 1385–1398), which unconditionally sets `DomainStatus.inactive`. This is exactly the purchased-but-stranded state the PR is designed to prevent. The PR correctly prevents re-throwing the raw `VercelError` on the last transient attempt, and it adds a helpful `logger.error` — but the post-loop timeout `Error` follows the same propagation path and triggers the same inactive update.

The test for budget exhaustion (`'retries a transient error on the final poll…'`) asserts `BadGatewayException` is thrown and the logger fires, but does **not** assert that `DomainStatus.inactive` was NOT written, so it does not protect against this path.

**Suggested fix**: throw a dedicated sentinel (e.g. `RegistrarOrderUnconfirmedError extends Error`) from here, then in the outer catch skip the `DomainStatus.inactive` update for that type. The exhaustion test should also add `expect(mockPrisma.domain.update).not.toHaveBeenCalledWith(expect.objectContaining({ data: { status: DomainStatus.inactive } }))`.

(Falsification check: the outer catch at lines 1385–1398 has no instanceof or error-type guard that would bypass the `DomainStatus.inactive` update for polling-timeout errors; verified no such guard exists.)

findings.body:
**`isVercelTransientError` likely misses bare `SDKError` instances — test failures and retry bypass at runtime.**

The method checks only `e instanceof VercelError`, but the tests at `vercel.service.test.ts` lines 102-106 assert that `new SDKError(...)` also returns `true`. The sibling-OR pattern in `isVercelNotFoundError` (`e instanceof NotFound || (e instanceof VercelError && ...)`) confirms `NotFound` and `VercelError` are siblings under `SDKError`, not parent-child — meaning `SDKError` does **not** extend `VercelError` and `instanceof VercelError` will not catch it.

At runtime, if `getRegistrarOrder` throws a bare `SDKError` with a 5xx/429 status, `isVercelTransientError` returns `false`, the loop re-throws immediately, and the domain is marked inactive — the exact regression this PR is meant to fix.

(Falsification check: if `SDKError` extended `VercelError`, the `NotFound || VercelError` OR in `isVercelNotFoundError` would be unnecessary since `NotFound` would also pass `instanceof VercelError`. The separate branches confirm they are siblings, not in a hierarchy that would make this check redundant.)

output.summary: This PR adds transient-error tolerance to the Vercel registrar-order polling loop, preventing a 502 during polling from stranding a paid domain purchase. The scout flagged three areas: (1) `isVercelTransientError` only checking `instanceof VercelError` while tests expect `SDKError` to also match, (2) the `lastPollTransientlyFailed` flag semantics in the mixed pending/transient scenario, and (3) an unbound method reference in a test. Deep review falsified leads 2 and 3 — the flag semantics are intentional (confirmed-Pending exhaustion correctly marks inactive) and the unbound method works because no `this` is used. Lead 1 (the SDKError gap from the prior round) remains: the `isVercelNotFoundError` sibling-OR pattern strongly suggests `SDKError` is the base class, so `instanceof VercelError` won't catch bare `SDKError` throws, and three unit tests plus the integration-style exhaustion test would fail. The prior finding about poll-exhaustion marking domains inactive (c98b2de5) has been fully addressed by `RegistrarOrderUnconfirmedError` and the outer-catch guard. The human reviewer should confirm the `@vercel/sdk` class hierarchy in node_modules to validate or close the remaining finding.
